A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VideoAuto-R1 and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-H. The corresponding material can be reliably matched without substantive reading gaps.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original model evaluations on video QA, grounding, and image benchmarks, together with training-strategy ablations and additional experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v2.pdf retains these original evaluations, ablations, training curves, and qualitative results, including those in the appendices.

M1.justification: The answer-think-answer procedure, dual-answer GRPO reward, fallback mechanism, and confidence-based early exit remain unchanged in Section 4 and Algorithm 1. No architecture or procedural component is introduced or removed.

E1.justification: The training sources in Appendix A and evaluation coverage remain the same: video QA, temporal grounding, grounding QA, and image reasoning. No dataset, domain, or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main and appendix experiments. Time-R1 remains in Table 4 with revised scores; the newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The stated model sizes, training settings, frame and token budgets, metrics, greedy decoding, 4,096-token response limit, and 0.97 threshold are retained. The new threshold-tuning description documents the existing setting rather than establishing a changed protocol.

E4.justification: The training-strategy and reward ablations, threshold sensitivity, data-filtering analysis, frame-count comparisons, grounding analysis, cold-start SFT experiments, and qualitative cases are retained. No analytical question or supporting experiment is added or removed.

E5.justification: Run-count, seed, uncertainty, and significance-reporting practices are unchanged. Replacing 93% and 87% with 0.93 and 0.87 in Section 5.3 is equivalent notation for model confidence, not a statistical reporting change.

E6.justification: Table 4 revises Time-R1's ActivityNet recall at IoU 0.3/0.5/0.7 and mIoU from 58.6/39.0/21.4/40.5 to 73.3/55.6/34.0/52.1, without explaining a setting change. This localized revision changes the reported ranking: Time-R1's mIoU now exceeds both VideoAuto-R1 variants, at 47.6 and 51.9. Other results, including appendix results, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The GRPO objective, confidence definition, reward formulas, Appendix B reward accounting, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about selective reasoning, dual-answer training, accuracy, and efficiency. The superiority claims are not narrowed following the Table 4 revision.

C2.justification: The explanations of when reasoning helps, confidence-based routing, limited grounding benefits, and limitations in Appendix G remain unchanged. Threshold generalization was already discussed in Sections 4.3 and 5.3; the revised baseline scores receive no corresponding reinterpretation.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 newly specifies that the 0.97 threshold was tuned on a small held-out validation subset and explicitly states that the existing 4,096-token limit avoids evaluation truncation. These are limited reporting additions; hardware, training details, prompts, and resource-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Sections 1 and 2.3 add five references: Adaptive Fast-and-Slow Visual Program Reasoning for Long-Form VideoQA, Aware First, Think Less, DAST, and two reasoning surveys. The surrounding contribution positioning remains unchanged; other citation-letter changes reflect bibliography relabeling.

P1.justification: There are localized edits to the evaluation-details paragraph, benchmark-name spellings, confidence notation, and citations. Section order, appendix organization, and the overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Added text and references cause minor paragraph and bibliography reflow, including an additional continuation line on page 9. Figures 1-11 and Tables 1-17 retain their designs and captions; Table 4's numerical revisions do not constitute a table redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful threshold-selection detail and broader citations. However, Table 4 raises Time-R1's ActivityNet mIoU from 40.5 to 52.1, above VideoAuto-R1's unchanged 47.6 and 51.9, while Section 5.2 still claims superiority over Time-R1. The unexplained score revision and unreconciled claim create a reporting inconsistency alongside the transparency gains, leaving the net quality effect unclear.
